questions.prompt: If a developer belongs to Group A allowing `s3:DeleteBucket` and also has an explicit policy statement denying `s3:DeleteBucket`, what happens when they call DeleteBucket?

options.text: AccessDenied: Explicit Deny always overrides any Allow statement
Allowed because Group permissions beat user permissions
The call succeeds only from CLI

questions.explanation: Explicit Deny takes absolute precedence across all policy evaluation stages.

questions.prompt: Why is OIDC federation preferable to saving long-lived static cloud access keys in GitHub Actions secrets?

options.text: Temporary STS tokens auto-expire quickly and are cryptographically bound to specific repositories/branches with zero static keys to leak
Static keys cannot upload files larger than 1MB
GitHub deletes static secrets after 1 hour

questions.explanation: Keyless federation eliminates credential rotation headaches and long-term secret leakage risks.

questions.prompt: Why do auto-scaling policies typically use shorter scale-out cooldowns (e.g., 60s) and longer scale-in cooldowns (e.g., 300s)?

options.text: To respond quickly to rising load while preventing premature capacity teardown during bumpy traffic lulls
Because scaling in triggers expensive license checks
Load balancers forbid adding nodes faster than removing them
To force CPU to remain permanently at 100%

questions.explanation: Fast scale-out preserves latency; conservative scale-in prevents oscillation thrashing.
